prompt: A school bus holds at most $40$ students. Write an inequality for the number of students $s$ that can ride. Write it like "s <= 40".
hint: Think about what "at most" allows. Is exactly $40$ students fine? Is $41$?

hints.text: Think about what "at most" allows. Is exactly $40$ students fine? Is $41$?
The count $s$ can be $40$ or any smaller number, so you need the symbol meaning "less than or equal to".
The inequality is $s \le 40$, which you type as "s <= 40".

explanation: "At most $40$" means the number of students can be $40$ or anything smaller, but never more.
The symbol for "less than or equal to" says exactly that, so the inequality is $s \le 40$.
The "or equal to" part matters because a bus with exactly $40$ students is still allowed, so the answer is "s <= 40".

alternativeExplanations.title: Test the boundary
steps: Can 40 students ride? Yes — "at most 40" allows exactly 40.
An inequality that says yes to 40 and no to 41 must be $s \le 40$.
